metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes; adjust downward bias for first 5–7 days.
- Overshoots after sharp upward sentiment moves (e.g., +0.50+ sentiment) — cap forecast peaks at 1–2% below true high if sentiment is positive.
- When sentiment is negative (avg < -0.4), model tends to overcorrect downward — add 0.5–1.0 to forecast to avoid excessive mean reversion.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 38.0), model should not forecast below 38.5 unless sentiment confirms strong bearish trend.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days of true values are trending upward, model should not forecast downward unless sentiment is explicitly bearish.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (avg -0.2 to 0.2), model should not overreact to recent volatility — use 3–5 day moving average of recent prices as baseline.
